questions: With sensors at ±0.03 m, does the weighted signal still respond cleanly through the bends, or does the wider spread reduce resolution near the centre line?
Did line_loss_events fall to zero on the s-bend and slalom, and at which progress point did any remaining loss occur?
Does max_error stay below 0.06 m, and on which track does the robot still leave the line?
If the robot now completes but steering_oscillation is high on the slalom, does reducing the forward lead to 0.03 m look like the next change?

intent: Widen the sensor spread from ±0.02 m to ±0.03 m, keeping 5 sensors, the 12 mm footprint, the 0.05 m forward lead and all body and wheel dimensions fixed. The aim is to stop line loss, which occurred on every track in iteration 0, by keeping the tape in view out to about 0.0485 m of lateral offset, before the 0.06 m off-track limit is reached. I expect line_loss_events to drop toward zero, max_error to stay below 0.06 m, and progress and completion to improve on the s-bend and slalom.
learning: Iteration 0 showed a 100% off-track failure with one line-loss event per trial, and the off-track limit is 0.06 m, not the body term. Hypotheses to test: (1) widening the spread to ±0.03 m removes line loss on the bends; (2) if line loss clears but steering oscillates, the forward lead is the next lever; (3) if the robot completes but is too slow, the wheel track or mass is the limit. Next I want line_loss_events, max_error, progress, completion_time and steering_oscillation from the race to confirm or reject hypothesis 1.
rationale: Iteration 0 raced the baseline with 5 sensors at x = ±0.02 m, 12 mm footprints, and y = 0.05 m. All 60 trials failed: every run ended off track, with 1 line-loss event each, max_error about 0.061 m, and progress only 0.04 to 0.115. No run finished. Two points matter. First, the off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.12/4) = max(0.06, 0.0425) = 0.06 m, so the 0.06 m floor binds, not the body term I cited in iteration 0. Max_error of about 0.061 m sits just past that limit, which confirms the robot drifts out of the tape band and the run ends. Second, line loss happens only when all sensors read below 0.05. With a 12 mm footprint and sensors at ±0.02 m, the outer sensors reach tape only up to roughly 0.0385 m of lateral offset. Beyond that the robot loses the line before it reaches the 0.06 m off-track limit, and the line-loss handling does not recover it. The Integrator's rule applies: line loss is above zero on every track, so the spread is too narrow to give recovery margin. I will widen the spread to ±0.03 m, keeping 5 sensors and the 12 mm footprint. That extends visibility to about 0.0485 m, so the sensors keep the tape in view further out and the robot has room to correct before losing it. I keep the forward lead at 0.05 m, because the lead should change only after the spread is addressed. I also keep wheel track, radius, mass and body fixed, so the race isolates the spread effect. Body width stays at 0.12 m: widening it to 0.18 m only moves the off-track term to about 0.0575 m, still below 0.06 m, so it gains nothing. Expected result: line_loss_events fall toward zero on the s-bend and slalom, max_error stays under 0.06 m, and progress rises well above 0.115.
